problem: 'किसी दूसरेके निहोरेसे' reads in modern Hindi as 'at anyone else's entreaty', which is not the verse's sense (आन निहोरें = for the sake of no one else) and differs from the English; निहोरा is also obscure to most readers.
fix: ऐसा सज्जन मेरे हृदयमें वैसे ही बसा रहता है जैसे लोभीके हृदयमें धन। तुम-जैसे संत मुझे प्रिय हैं; किसी औरके लिये मैं देह धारण नहीं करता।

problem: Ungrammatical: a comma separates subject and verb ('… observances, are'), and the last clause dangles ('…to me, those who love…'). 'Worship the Lord' in Śrī Rāma's own mouth is also odd (Hindi: सगुण रूपके उपासक).
fix: Those who worship God with form and attributes, who are intent on the good of others and firm in right conduct and in their observances: such men, who love the feet of brāhmaṇas, are as dear to me as my own life.

problem: In 'जो अपनी ही साँसकी … हवासे भड़क उठी थी' अपनी grammatically binds to जो (the fire), so the Hindi does not keep the ambiguity the doubt claims; it also leaves out जी for Vibhīṣaṇa after refuge (style §6) and reorders the verse more than needed.
fix: रावणका क्रोध आग था और अपनी ही साँस उसे भड़कानेवाली प्रचंड हवा; उसमें जलते हुए विभीषणजीको श्रीरामजीने बचा लिया और अखण्ड राज्य दे दिया।

problem: Narration after Vibhīṣaṇa has taken refuge: style §6 gives विभीषणजी (the batch uses विभीषणजी in 49.cau2 and 51.cau4, plain विभीषण here).
fix: जो सम्पत्ति शिवजीने रावणको उसके दस सिर चढ़ानेपर दी थी, वही सम्पदा श्रीरघुनाथजीने सकुचाते हुए विभीषणजीको दी।

problem: विभीषणजी in narration after refuge (style §6).
fix: जो ऐसे प्रभुको छोड़कर किसी औरका भजन करते हैं, वे मनुष्य बिना पूँछ-सींगके पशु हैं। विभीषणजीको अपना जन जानकर प्रभुने अपना लिया; प्रभुका यह स्वभाव सारे वानरकुलको मन भाया।

problem: विभीषणजी in narration after refuge (style §6).
fix: लंकापति विभीषणजीने कहा — हे रघुनाथजी! सुनिये, आपका बाण करोड़ों समुद्रोंको सोख लेनेवाला है। फिर भी नीतिमें ऐसा कहा गया है कि जाकर समुद्रसे विनती की जाय।

problem: The ocean is approached and entreated as a person here: style §6 'the Ocean'.
fix: Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, said: O Lord of the Raghus, listen. Your arrow could dry up ten million oceans. Even so, policy teaches that one should go to the Ocean and make a humble request.

problem: सागर is 'the ocean' (style §6); 'the sea' breaks the batch's own usage.
fix: My Lord, the Ocean is a revered elder of your line. He will think it over and tell you a way, and the entire army of bears and monkeys will get across the ocean without effort.

problem: 'हाल सुना' (imperative of सुनाना) reads first as the past 'heard'; the verse has कहु. Use an unambiguous imperative.
fix: उस मूर्खने राज करते हुए लंकाको छोड़ दिया; अब वह अभागा जौके साथ पिसनेवाला घुन बनेगा। फिर भालुओं और वानरोंकी उस सेनाका हाल बता, जो निर्दय कालकी प्रेरणासे चलकर यहाँ आ गयी है।

problem: Rāvaṇa speaks of the ocean as a person (poor, soft-hearted, guardian): style §6 'the Ocean'.
fix: That poor soft-hearted Ocean has become the guardian of their lives. And then tell me about those ascetics, whose hearts are full of dread of me.

problem: 'ही' (the troop-leaders alone) is not in the verse (पदुम अठारह जूथप बंदर); also a colon is not our Hindi punctuation (use कि).
fix: हे रावण! मैंने अपने कानोंसे ऐसा सुना है कि वानरोंके यूथपतियोंकी गिनती अठारह पद्म है। उस सेनामें, हे नाथ! एक भी वानर ऐसा नहीं, जो रणमें आपको जीत न ले।

problem: 'alone' is not in the verse.
fix: This I have heard with my own ears, Rāvaṇa: the monkey troop-leaders number eighteen padmas (a padma being an immense number). In that army, my lord, there is no monkey who would not defeat you in battle.

problem: The ocean is asked for a way as a person: 'the Ocean' (style §6).
fix: On his advice he is asking the Ocean for a way across, with mercy in his heart. Hearing this, Rāvaṇa laughed: With wits like these, no wonder he has made monkeys his allies.

problem: The ocean is pestered as a person: 'the Ocean' (style §6).
fix: Relying on the word of a born coward, he has taken to sulking and pestering the Ocean like a spoilt child. Fool, why do you sing false praises? I have taken the measure of my enemy's strength and wit.

problem: Lakṣmaṇa's letter, so honorifics apply: style §6 gives ब्रह्माजी, शिवजी (the batch writes शिवजी in 49.cau4 and 49.do49ख).
fix: अरे मूर्ख! बातोंसे ही मन बहलाकर अपने वंशको मिट्टीमें न मिला। श्रीरामजीसे वैर ठानकर तू बच नहीं पायेगा, चाहे भगवान् विष्णु, ब्रह्माजी और शिवजीकी शरण ले ले।

problem: The Hindi heading follows Gita Press's heading point by point and ends in nearly their words (लक्ष्मणजीका पत्र लेकर लौटना ~ लक्ष्मणजीके पत्रको लेकर लौटना). 'लक्ष्मणजीका … लौटना' can also be misread as Lakṣmaṇa returning. The English is fine.
fix: समुद्र कैसे पार हो, इसपर विचार; रावणके दूतोंका पकड़ा जाना और लक्ष्मणजीका उन्हें पत्र देकर छुड़ाना

problem: Agree it is a genuine doubt. The entry should give the argument for the epithet reading: प्रतिपालक stands in a run of agent-noun epithets of the Lord ending in the rhyming घालक; Gita Press takes it of the words, as we do.
fix: {"id": "sundar.50.cau2", "issue": "नीति प्रतिपालक: an epithet of the Lord (upholder of right counsel) or a description of his words (words that uphold right counsel)?", "our reading": "Of the words: 'नीतिकी रक्षा करनेवाले वचन' / 'words that upheld right counsel'.", "alternatives": "As one more epithet of the Lord, 'नीतिके पालक प्रभु' / 'the upholder of right counsel': प्रतिपालक is an agent noun like the other epithets in the list and rhymes with घालक."}

problem: Missing doubt: we take बलरासि of Jāmbavān alone ('बलकी राशि जाम्बवान्'); Gita Press reads it of all the warriors named ('ये सभी बलकी राशि हैं'). The words allow both.
